title: Groomed - review of play by Patrick Sandford
transcript: welcome to one minute theater reviews I'm Paul seven Louis and this is my review of groomed by Patrick Sanford and available at Soho Theatre on demand calm the adult tries so hard to forget but the child always remembers saves the protagonist I'm sure you will be as sad and angry as I was by the end of this 50 minute monologue about the abuse suffered by a ten-year-old child and the reverberating effect it has had on the rest of his life it's exceptional impact is tribute to the writing and acting of the former artistic director of the novel Southampton Patrick Santha takes us on a Gideon ride as well as the story of what happened in that classroom he tells us stories from the ancient classics history of the saxophone the story of the Japanese soldier who carried on fighting for 29 years after the world war had ended all providing metaphors for his experience and how it can be faced well that's the one-minute review keep watching for more about Patrick's anthems devastating play groomed although written for the stage this is a filmed version directed by Nancy Meckler and as with Andrew Scott in Sewall having one person talking directly to you through the camera seems to me to come closest to the experience of theatre the film also takes the opportunity to place our protagonist in a primary school classroom the scene of the crime if you like most heartbreaking is the gradual revelation of the damage that the experience has inflicted on the adult the fear the shame the guilt the bad done to me becomes the bad in me becomes the bad is me he says and like a tide that goes out and comes in again we keep returning to the child and his awful experience at the hands of his teacher there are no details he's very clear that this isn't fodder for sensational tabloids the shock is not in what happened but how it happened and how the grooming was allowed to happen and how there were apparently no consequences for the teacher and he even takes his a little way inside the head of the teacher it's so upsetting that this should happen to a fellow human being that you almost want to block it out just as you now might want to avoid seeing this play but patrick stanford stares at you defying you both in his words and in his piercing eyes to look away and there is hope in talking about it rage that his herd transforms to mighty trees he says and talks of the alchemy of anger into trust I understand now much more than I did about the way in which the experience of abuse is never something historical but rather something ever-present in the life as someone who was abused so it is educational but groomed is so successful as a drama because Patrick understands the power of theatre as a cathartic experience and the way it can elicit empathy as well as sympathy open my heart for me he says to us and even in these times of social distancing it made me want to hug him I give groomed five stars I hope you found this review useful and
